strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub- strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify sites for soil improvement in the school or community b) Construct organic waste pit for soil improvement c) Demonstrate use of plant remains for soil improvement.
strands.experiences: Learners are guided to:  Discuss and identify sites in the school or community that have poor soil for crop growth.  Construct a pit, a site or a structure for damping plant residue and suitable food remains and organic kitchen wastes in school.  Plant crop in a residue pit to observe and appreciate soil improvement from accumulated organic wastes.  Learners to develop observation skills as they identify appropriate site, value of unity as they work to construct the pit and environmental awareness while recycling organic wastes in the pit method to improve the soil.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can we improve the soil using suitable organic wastes?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify ways of conserving water for household gardening b) Practice water conservation within the school or community c) Appreciate importance of conserving water in the community.
strands.experiences: Learners are guided to:  Use devices or other resources to search for information on ways of water conservation such as mulching, cover cropping and shading in kitchen and backyard gardening.  Make presentations to share experiences on importance of conserving water (mulching, cover cropping and shading) in kitchen and backyard gardening activities.  Practice various ways of conserving water in farming (Mulching, shading, cover cropping) within the school.  In groups learners to experiment on mulching (mulch some crops and leave others un-mulched and compare moisture conservation).  Learners develop learning to learn by engaging in self-driven task of water conservation, responsible use of devices
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can we conserve soil water in household gardening practices?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify ways of repelling wild animals to avoid damage of property b) Repel wild animals to avoid destruction of property c) Appreciate importance of living better with wild animals.
strands.experiences: Learners are guided to:  Watch video clips or listen to a resource person on safe ways of repelling wild animals (such as use of smoke, smells) to avoid damage on property (crops and domestic animals) and live better with wild animals.  Innovate safe ways of repelling small wild animals (smoke, use of smell repellant or any other).  Learners develop critical thinking skills to solve the problem of destruction of property, demonstrating value of patriotism (love) for the environment by living better with wild animals and care for biodiversity.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can we repel wild animals to avoid destruction of property?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify gardening practices for vegetables b) Establish a nursery bed for vegetables c) Grow vegetable crop after transplanting d) Appreciate the importance of vegetables in provision healthy meals diet.
strands.experiences: Learners are guided to:  Brainstorm and share experiences on gardening practices of vegetables in a nursery bed.  Prepare a nursery bed (container or ground nursery), sow vegetable seed and take care of the seedling.  Make class presentations importance of growing vegetables as a source of food for animals and humans.  Learners develop self-efficacy in producing their own vegetable foods, the value of social justice in sharing of tasks, and financial literacy skills by reducing daily vegetable purchases.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How does growing vegetables contribute to food production?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify uses of various domestic animals in food production b) Relate various domestic animals to their uses c) Appreciate the importance of domestic animals in food production.
strands.experiences: Learners are guided to:  Brainstorm and share experiences on the uses of domestic animals in food production (bees, rabbits, camels, fish, pigs, donkeys, dogs and cats).  Match domestic animals to their uses.  Make class presentations on importance of domestic animals in food production while relating contributions of all the scoped animals.  Learners develop communication skills as they present the uses of domestic animals, patriotism as they appreciate diversity of animals in the country, and appreciate importance of animals in food security.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How are domestic animals important in food production?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Describe methods of preserving cereals and pulses the locality b) Preserve cereals and pulses for food security c) Appreciate the importance of preserving cereals and pulses for food security.
strands.experiences: Learners are guided to:  Brainstorm and share experiences on methods of preserving and storing cereals and pulses (such as sun drying, use of ashes, use of airtight containers) at household level.  Preserve and store cereals and pulses using methods such as sun drying, use of ash and airtight containers.  Make class presentations to share experiences on importance of preserving and storing cereals and pulses.  Learners develop critical thinking skills to solve the problem of food spoilage, the value of unity and team work as learners make class presentations and food security awareness in preserving foods.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How does preservation and storage of cereals and pulses enhance food security?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Explain functions of food nutrients in the body b) Categorize foods based on their major nutrients c) Appreciate the importance of various nutrients in the body.
strands.experiences: Learners are guided to:  Search and share information on functions of food nutrients (carbohydrates, vitamins, proteins, fats).  Use real food materials, photographs, to categorize foods based on their major nutrients (protein rich foods, carbohydrates rich foods, vitamins and minerals rich foods).  Make class presentations on the importance of various nutrients in the body.  Learners develop digital literacy as they search for information on nutrients, value of unity as they make presentations and health promotion as they learn about the importance of nutrients in the body.
strands.inquiryQuestions: Why is the knowledge of food nutrients important in food production?

strands.subStrand: Dry Fat Frying and Deep Frying
strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Describe dry fat frying and deep frying as methods of cooking b) Cook food using dry fat frying and deep frying methods c) Embrace dry fat frying and deep frying in food production.
strands.experiences: Learners are guided to:  Watch video clip or demonstration on dry fat frying and deep frying methods of cooking.  Cook and serve dry fried and deep fried foods.  Learners develop learning to learn while working cautiously to dry frying and deep frying processes, working resiliently while following cooking steps, promoting safety measures while working with fire and fats.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can we cook foods using dry fat frying and deep frying methods?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Describe good grooming as a daily health habit b) Practice good grooming as a daily health habit c) Appreciate good grooming as a healthy habit.
strands.experiences: Learners are guided to:  Discuss and share experiences on aspects of good grooming such dressing for different occasions.  Demonstrate different ways of dressing and etiquette for different activities.  Adopt good grooming while carrying out daily chores.  Learners develop self-confidence while promoting good grooming, respect (open mindedness) in appreciating others and personal hygiene to promote preventive health.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How does good grooming promote personal hygiene?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify surfaces made from different materials in home environment b) Clean different types of surfaces in the home environment c) Appreciate living in a clean home environment to promote healthy living.
strands.experiences: Learners are guided to:  Discuss and share experiences on surfaces made from different materials such as glass, wooden, earthen floors, cemented and tiled.  Clean different types of surfaces such as glass, wooden, earthen floors, cemented and tiled.  Learners develop listening and speaking skills while brainstorming, unity while cleaning surfaces and safety while they take personal care in the cleaning activity.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How do you clean surfaces made from different materials?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Describe how to launder a cotton item b) Launder a cotton item for personal hygiene c) Appreciate importance of laundry work for hygiene purposes.
strands.experiences: Learners are guided to:  Watch a clip or observe a demonstration on how to launder a cotton item (white and fast coloured cotton).  Launder a white and fast coloured cotton item.  Practice laundering of white and fast coloured items at home to appreciate the importance of laundry work for personal hygiene.  Learners develop learning to learn as they adopt learnt skills to launder personal items, responsibility while taking care of the personal items and hygiene promotion by maintaining cleanliness.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How does laundering cotton items promote hygiene?

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Identify stiches used in repairing garment b) Make samples of stiches used to repair garments c) Use the stiches to repair gapping seam d) Adopt the stitches to repair of garments.
strands.experiences: Learners are guided to:  Use pictures, realia, video clips and charts to identify stiches such as back stitch and running stitch used in repairing garment  Make samples of running and back stitch.  Use back stitch and running stitch to repair gapping seam.  Adopt the stitches to repair their daily wear.  Learners develop problem solving skills as they repair their garments, responsibility as learners take care of their clothes and financial literacy as learners save costs of repairs.

strands.outcomes: By the end of the sub strand the learner should be able to: a) Distinguish between horizontal and vertical innovative gardening b) Construct vertical and horizontal gardens for growing crop c) Adopt the use of vertical and horizontal gardens in growing crops.
strands.experiences:  Learners watch or observe stimulus materials (video clips, pictures, and photographs) on innovative gardening practices showing various crops in innovative gardens (vertical and horizontal gardens).  Learners to use sacks, plastic bottles, walls, plastic pipes among others to construct vertical and horizontal gardens for growing crops.  Learners use the vertical and horizontal gardens to grow appropriate crop.  Creativity and innovation skills as learners design and construct the gardens, team work as the learners construct the gardens and problems solving as learners solve pertinent problem of space for growing crops.
strands.inquiryQuestions: How can gardening be done on vertical and horizontal spaces?
